extracted.intended_audience: stakeholders, commenters, and members of the public searching Federal Register documents about net neutrality and related federal policy
extracted.subtask_description: Search-results collection of Federal Register documents matching the term "net neutrality," aggregating excerpts from notices, proposed/final rules, and other FR entries that mention net neutrality and related policy terms (e.g., budget neutrality, gender neutrality).

rubrics_metrics.name: Socially Vulnerable Communities (15 points)
rubrics_metrics.description: For applications where at least 75 percent of the PFSA(s) are proposing to serve Socially Vulnerable Communities, as defined in this notice, 15 points will be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a scored criterion in the Rural eConnectivity (ReConnect) funding opportunity announcement; applicants must meet the 75% PFSA threshold (PFSA defined in the FOA) to receive the 15-point credit. See FOA for the FOA's definition of Socially Vulnerable Communities and any required supporting documentation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Net neutrality commitment (10 points) — FOA scoring
rubrics_metrics.description: For applicants that commit to net neutrality principles, 10 points will be awarded.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Applicants must submit a board resolution or equivalent in the application committing that the applicant's networks shall not (a) block lawful content, applications, services, or non-harmful devices (excerpt truncated). This is an application-scoring criterion in the ReConnect FOA; the submission of the resolution/equivalent is required to claim the points.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on blocking, throttling, and paid/affiliated prioritization (FCC rule)
rubrics_metrics.description: Reinstated rules that prohibit blocking, throttling, or engaging in paid or affiliated prioritization arrangements for broadband internet access service.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Part of the FCC's 'Restoring Internet Freedom' Report and Order context: these are explicit, straightforward prohibitions imposed on broadband providers. They function as regulatory constraints on provider behavior; the rule text defines the scope of prohibited actions and enforcement mechanisms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Transparency rule enhancements (FCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adoption of certain enhancements to the transparency rule for broadband providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Enhancements require providers to disclose network practices (e.g., traffic management, performance metrics) to increase consumer and regulator visibility. The rule changes append to the prohibitions on conduct and are implemented alongside classification/forbearance decisions.

rubrics_metrics.name: General conduct standard prohibiting unreasonable interference or unreasonable disadvantage (FCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: A general conduct standard that prohibits unreasonable interference or unreasonable disadvantage to consumers or edge providers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This standard operates in addition to specific prohibitions (blocking/throttling/prioritization) to capture harm not directly addressed by enumerated rules. It is a legal/regulatory standard used to evaluate provider conduct and to support enforcement.

rubrics_metrics.name: Classification of broadband internet access service as a Title II telecommunications service (FCC)
rubrics_metrics.description: Classifying broadband internet access service (BIAS) as a telecommunications service under Title II of the Communications Act to provide the Commission with authority over BIAS.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a statutory/regulatory designation that establishes the FCC's authority to promulgate and enforce the above prohibitions and standards. The Order may also adopt broad, tailored forbearance from certain Title II provisions while retaining those provisions necessary to fulfill statutory objectives (e.g., public safety, consumer protection).

rubrics_metrics.name: Gender-neutral language / inclusive pronoun usage (GSA FMR/FTR amendments)
rubrics_metrics.description: Technical amendments replace gender-specific pronouns (e.g., he, she, his, her) with non-gendered pronouns to result in more inclusive language.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These are editorial/style amendments to the Federal Management Regulation and Federal Travel Regulation; they are grammatical and technical in nature and do not change substantive policy or add costs. Implementers should substitute non-gendered pronouns across affected parts and correct minor grammatical/administrative errors as indicated.

rubrics_metrics.name: PAYGO deficit-neutrality requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: The PAYGO Act requires deficit neutrality: provisions must produce outlay changes that net to zero over the current year, budget year, and the four subsequent years; off-budget effects are not counted as budgetary effects.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: OMB issues an annual PAYGO report and, if necessary, a sequestration order. Implementation uses two scorecards that tally cumulative budgetary effects; off-budget items (Social Security trust funds, Postal Service) are excluded from PAYGO calculations.

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget-neutrality adjustment for Medicare/healthcare payment updates
rubrics_metrics.description: Changes to wage index values, case-mix weights, CMG relative weights, and similar payment updates must be applied in a budget-neutral manner so total estimated payments are unchanged; agencies apply a budget-neutrality factor.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Federal Register excerpts describe steps and examples: calculate estimated total payments without changes, calculate payments with proposed changes, and apply a budget-neutrality factor to the standardized amount (or otherwise) so aggregate payments remain the same. This is used across IPPS, IRF, IPF, ESRD PPS, and other Medicare payment systems; documentation in each rule explains the exact computation and the factors applied.
